messages:
sanjay: heads up — seeing a weird pattern in eu-west1: lots of small 1GPU jobs pending while there are nodes with free GPU slots. scheduler seems to be leaving 1-2 GPUs unused per node.
talia: is this the same 'fragmentation' we've seen before or something new?
sanjay: feels different. this started after the scheduler-weight-tuning rollout yesterday. suspect pod topologySpread + soft-affinity are interacting poorly.
noah: can you paste a quick `kubectl get pods` + `kubectl describe node` for one example?
sanjay: yeah, grabbing now.
ops-bot: snapshot created: cluster/eu-west1 at 2026-03-20T10:16:39Z :white_check_mark:
sanjay: ```
$ kubectl get pods -n ml-workloads | grep Pending
model-train-abc   0/1 Pending  0  3m
preproc-1        0/1 Pending  0  2m

$ kubectl describe node gpu-node-17 | egrep "Allocatable:|Allocated:|Taints:"
Allocatable: nvidia.com/gpu=8
Allocated: nvidia.com/gpu=7
Taints: nvidia.com/gpu-dedicated:NoSchedule
```
maya: allocated 7/8 but pending look like they still can't bind — maybe kube-scheduler sees fragmentation because of topologySpread constraints?
noah: if Allocated=7 and there's still pending, that means the free slot is isolated by constraints (affinity/taints/limits). check `podSpec.affinity` and `nodeSelector`.
stian: (typo) meant sanjay — I see a bunch of jobs with `preferredDuringScheduling` anti-affinity that have high weight since we increased the weight yesterday. they become effectively hard.
talia: ohhh, the weight change in scheduler-configmap bumped preferredDuringScheduling to 100 in our rollout? that would make them act like required.
ryan: we set `preferredDuringScheduling` weight -> 100 to reduce noisy co-location for some teams, but forgot that several ML jobs use that field to avoid same-node placement for internal replicas. consequence: scheduler fragments.
sanjay: proposed quick fixes: 1) revert weight change in scheduler config to previous (canary first) 2) run descheduler to coalesce small pods onto partially used nodes 3) add a packing score plugin override for gpu profiles. thoughts?
maya: 1) + do a canary revert in eu-west1 only. 2) descheduler -> prefer `RemovePodsViolatingInterPodAntiAffinity` and `LowNodeUtilization` policies.
noah: agree. also consider temporary admission-controller tweak to ignore the preferred anti-affinity for low-priority ML batch jobs (nicer than rollback if we need time).	alia: I'm +1 for canary revert. I'll prepare the kustomize patch and a quick rollback playbook.
ops-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/scheduler-weight-rollout ; next step owner: talia
ryan: also want metrics to verify: node gpu fragmentation (free_slots distribution), pending_by_reason, scheduler_score_histogram. I can add dashboards.
sanjay: will scale down some stray 1GPU dev fleets to free a few nodes as immediate relief.
talia: scheduling revert patch in PR 4213, canary deploying to eu-west1 now. ping when live.
noah: once canary is live i'll watch pending count and scheduling decisions for 10m.
sanjay: thanks — keeping this thread for status. :thumbsup:
